brief: Goldman estimates the global oil deficit narrowed from about 7mb/d near the war's start in March to about 1mb/d in Q3, as Gulf output partially recovered, demand weakened and non-Middle East supply rose faster than expected. JPMorgan puts non-Middle East production up about 2mb/d in H1 2026, 700kb/d above its forecast, and puts global consumption about 5mb/d below year-ago levels since the Hormuz disruption. It expects Chinese demand to fall from 17.3mb/d in 2025 to 16.6mb/d in 2026. Goldman sees Venezuelan output reaching 1.9mb/d by 2030 and 2.3mb/d by 2035 as Chevron lifts production toward 600kb/d and fiscal reform cuts breakevens to about $58 a barrel. The heavier, sourer crude could support Gulf Coast refining margins while adding diesel supply if demand stays soft. JPMorgan models Brent at $87 in 2027 even if the conflict persists, versus $63 in its peace scenario, while Goldman's base case is $80. The note argues no further escalation, not peace, is now the bearish catalyst. TME calls oil mean-reverting and warns CTA long positioning creates downside asymmetry if trend levels break. Goldman recommends expressing further downside through the USO Oct 140/120 put spread, about 4x max payout.
